candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Case Management/Collaboration/Continuity of Care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — case management and continuity
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize case management as individualized coordination of services and transitions across settings.

options.A: Coordinate referrals, services, equipment, and transition needs across settings according to the client's individualized goals and plan of care.
options.B: Perform all bedside procedures personally and leave coordination with community and specialty services to other disciplines.
options.C: Arrange the same standardized services for every client without incorporating individual goals, preferences, or changing needs.
options.D: Postpone resource planning and transition coordination until after the client has already been discharged.

candidate.rationale: Case management emphasizes individualized coordination, continuity, resource linkage, communication, and transitions across the care continuum. A reflects those functions. B narrows the role to direct procedures, C ignores individualized planning, and D delays coordination until after the transition has occurred.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Management of Care includes coordinating client care, resources, referrals, continuity, and transitions.
candidate.source_locator: Management of Care — Case Management, Collaboration, and Continuity of Care activity statements
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
